P01-008.boundary_rationale: Onset: 4:1 וְאַתָּ֤ה בֶן אָדָם֙ קַח לְךָ֣ לְבֵנָ֔ה (oshb:Ezek.4.1) (“You also, son of man, take a tile” (web:Ezek.4.1)), the 'and you, son of man' sub-onset that stands at the head of the collection this row opens (one of the book's 23 occurrences of that construction), immediately after the parent seam at oshb:Ezek.3.27. The same siege-tile complex continues through the lying sign-acts at 4:4 and the food-rationing at 4:9 without a matching 'son of man' sub-onset at either point (both open with the bare 've'attah' alone), so all three stages read as one commanded symbolic act rather than three. At 4:8, וְהִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי עָלֶ֖יךָ עֲבוֹתִ֑ים (oshb:Ezek.4.8) (“Behold, I put ropes on you” (web:Ezek.4.8)) takes up the ropes again: the same consonantal word stands at 3:25, pointed differently there, and that continuity is disclosed here as evidence for the seam this row opens on and not for any cut inside it. A second address at 4:16, בֶּן אָדָם֙ (oshb:Ezek.4.16), intensifies rather than restarts the act (“behold, I will break the staff of bread” (web:Ezek.4.16)). Close: 4:17, לְמַ֥עַן יַחְסְר֖וּ לֶ֣חֶם וָמָ֑יִם (oshb:Ezek.4.17) (“that they may lack bread and water” (web:Ezek.4.17)), with a pe recorded after it (single-witness), before 5:1 opens a distinct sign-act with its own 'son of man' address.
P01-008.device_notes: Whole-chapter span disclosed: the unit runs 17 verses, over the 7-10 verse target, and is kept whole rather than forced into an unsupported cut, since no formula-marked seam stands between 4:3/4:4 or 4:8/4:9. Two K/Q verses checked before quoting (4:6, 4:15); 4:6 also carries an editorial note tied to the same disputed consonant, disclosed together. Paseq at 4:9 disclosed count-only, single-witness. MT 3:27 is followed by a samekh (single-witness); the sign-act series that opens at 4:1 has this mark standing immediately before it. Inside the span a samekh follows MT 4:12 (single-witness); the unit does not cut there because the food-rationing act begun at 4:9 continues without a fresh 'son of man' address or messenger formula reopening the speech. A further samekh stands after MT 4:14 (single-witness) inside the span; no cut is made there either, since 4:15's concession is Yahweh's reply within the same rationing scene, not a fresh address. A samekh also follows MT 4:15 (single-witness), inside the span as well; no cut is made there, because the address at 4:16 intensifies the rationing act rather than restarting it.

P02-009.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.11.14 וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר, the strict word-event formula (one of the book's 39 strict-form onsets), opens an oracle addressed to the exiles rather than to the courtyard men of Ezek.11.1-11.13 — an addressee-class shift inside the vision, from the Jerusalem claimants (oshb:Ezek.11.15, which the WEB renders “This land has been given to us for a possession.” (web:Ezek.11.15)) to “your brothers… the house of Israel” (web:Ezek.11.15) in exile. The witness records a pe after MT 11:13 (single witness), at the seam this unit opens on at 11:14. Close: oshb:Ezek.11.21 וְאֶל לֵ֧ב שִׁקּוּצֵיהֶ֛ם וְתוֹעֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֖ם לִבָּ֣ם הֹלֵ֑ךְ דַּרְכָּם֙ בְּרֹאשָׁ֣ם נָתַ֔תִּי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה ends with the utterance formula נאם אדני יהוה (one of the book's 81 utterance-close verses). The close seam is two-faced: the utterance signature ends 11:21 and the vision's return to the prophet opens at 11:22. The onset's far face is not: MT 11:13 ends on the prophet's own cry and carries no close-role formula, and the pe recorded after it corroborates the paragraph without supplying one. That one bare far face is the evidence this row's confidence reports. This embedded salvation oracle stands inside the still-open vision (the courtyard scene has not yet returned the prophet — that happens only at 11:22-25) but is bounded by its own onset and close formulae independent of the vision frame, so it is set as its own row rather than folded into 11:1-13 or 11:22-25.
P02-009.device_notes: Filed under the restoration promise that is the unit's burden (gather-and-return is stated here: MEASURED at oshb:Ezek.11.17, the oracle both gathers and gives the land — the consonantal skeleton carries וקבצתי אתכם מן העמים ואספתי אתכם מן הארצות and ונתתי לכם את אדמת ישראל, which the WEB renders “I will gather you from the peoples, and assemble you out of the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” (web:Ezek.11.17) — and the “one heart… heart of flesh” (web:Ezek.11.19) promise stands alongside it, so that filing rests on the device the unit actually carries); a one-sentence deviation is disclosed because the unit also carries a disputation-oracle color (the quoted Jerusalem claim at 11:15 is refuted before the promise is given), and the category is not read as free text beyond that single disclosure. No K/Q or paseq falls in this span.

P02-018.boundary_rationale: Onset: oshb:Ezek.13.17 וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֗ם שִׂ֤ים פָּנֶ֨יךָ֙ אֶל בְּנ֣וֹת עַמְּךָ֔ הַמִּֽתְנַבְּא֖וֹת מִֽלִּבְּהֶ֑ן וְהִנָּבֵ֖א עֲלֵיהֶֽן — “set your face against the daughters of your people” (web:Ezek.13.17) — is one of the book's 9 set-your-face verses and marks an addressee-class shift from the male prophets of 13:1-16 to women “who prophesy out of their own heart” (web:Ezek.13.17). Close: oshb:Ezek.13.23 לָכֵ֗ן שָׁ֚וְא לֹ֣א תֶחֱזֶ֔ינָה וְקֶ֖סֶם לֹא תִקְסַ֣מְנָה ע֑וֹד וְהִצַּלְתִּ֤י אֶת עַמִּי֙ מִיֶּדְכֶ֔ן וִֽידַעְתֶּ֖ן כִּֽי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה ends “Then you will know that I am Yahweh.” (web:Ezek.13.23) in the second-feminine-plural form (וידעתן), a counted form of its own (sweep: 2 verses) that belongs to neither the 3mp-28 nor the 2mp-21 recognition class, though both of its verses are members of the wide recognition family (sweep: 64 verses), whose members are refrain-grade close evidence; a matching 2fp clause also closes the magic-bands sub-paragraph at oshb:Ezek.13.21. Both sides: a pe follows oshb:Ezek.13.16 immediately before this row's onset (single-witness), so the onset's near face is the set-your-face command with its change of addressee and its far face is 13:16's verse-final signature. The close's near face is the counted 2fp recognition form at 13:23, refrain-grade through that wide family in its two-verse form rather than the 3mp or 2mp class, and across that seam a new scene opens at 14:1, where the elders of Israel come and sit before the prophet — a turn read on the text rather than counted in any formula class, and the far-face signal this grade rests on. No interior seam is licensed against it: the one weighed below opens on no fresh onset.

P02-020.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting at oshb:Ezek.14.20, where a pe falls after the fourth triad refrain (single-witness) and immediately before the oracle turns from the hypothetical four scourges to their explicit application to Jerusalem (14:21-23), is the standing rival, and it is weighed here rather than passed over. MT 14:21 opens with a messenger formula: MEASURED on this witness's consonantal skeleton, oshb:Ezek.14.21 begins כי כה אמר אדני יהוה, and that verse is among the 122 verses that carry the long messenger formula. What it opens is nonetheless a paragraph, not a sub-onset, since a messenger sub-onset is granted only where the addressee changes or where the verse just before it ENDS on a close-role formula, and neither condition is met. Nothing marks a new addressee at 14:21 — MEASURED, the son-of-man address falls at MT 14:3 and MT 14:13 and at no other verse of this chapter, chapter 14 carries no set-your-face verse at all, and 14:21 is not opened by 'and you, son of man' — so what turns there is the subject, from a hypothetical land to Jerusalem, and not the person addressed. As for the second condition, the utterance formula in MT 14:20 does NOT reach the verse end: MEASURED, נאם אדני יהוה sits at characters 29 through 41 of an 81-character skeleton, the first character counted as 1 and both ends included, and from there the oath's own content runs to the etnachta, with אם בן אם בת יצילו המה בצדקתם יצילו נפשם standing between that signature and the sof pasuq, its second clause independent after the major disjunctive. So the pe on MT 14:20 is entered as support for the rival it favours and for no more than that: this witness records the break after MT 14:20, a mark cannot supply the verse-final close-role formula that the second condition asks for, and paragraph evidence informs while every licensed driver outranks it. The row carries on to its own verse-final utterance close at oshb:Ezek.14.23.
P02-020.device_notes: MT 14:14 and MT 14:20 both carry the Qere-adaptation editorial note class disclosed above, in addition to the ordinary ketiv/qere note at each verse (ketiv דנאל, qere דָּנִיֵּ֣אל (oshb:Ezek.14.14 and oshb:Ezek.14.20) — the shorter legendary-figure spelling against the fuller ‘Daniel’ reading); both disclosures are given at both verses since they are two independent single-witness apparatus facts about the same word. Paseq at 14:21 is count-only, single-witness. oshb:Ezek.15.1 is cited above only as forward-side onset evidence for the seam; it is not a row here. Length disclosure: this row is 12 verses (MEASURED: web:Ezek.14.12-Ezek.14.23, tallied on the WEB face) against a 7-10 verse target length. The over-length is disclosed and carried rather than hidden: the four-scourge refrain list is never cut inside itself, and the one internal seam a reader might take, the messenger paragraph at 14:21, is weighed and held in the rejected alternative.

P03-003.boundary_rationale: Onset side: no formula device opens MT 16:15; the row continues the word-event unit framed at 16:1 by default, picking up the narrative turn וַתִּבְטְחִ֣י בְיָפְיֵ֔ךְ וַתִּזְנִ֖י (oshb:Ezek.16.15) — the WEB reads “But you trusted in your beauty, and played the prostitute because of your renown” (web:Ezek.16.15) — immediately after 16:14's close. Close side: this row's final verse is 16:19; its concluding clause is the utterance formula וַיֶּ֑הִי נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.16.19) ('so it happened, declares the Lord YHWH'), closing the account of the gifts turned into idol-offerings before the child-sacrifice material opens at 16:20 with its own fresh clause. The onset's near face carries no formula device at all, a turn in the account read rather than counted, and its far face at 16:14 ends verse-final on the utterance formula; the close rests on 16:19's verse-final formula alone, with no parashah mark anywhere in this five-verse stretch (sweep: 5 verses) to corroborate it, single-witness. The unlicensed near face at the onset is what this row's reduced confidence records. MT 16:18 (oshb:Ezek.16.18) carries a single Ketiv/Qere note inside this span: the running text reads the ketiv נתתי in place of the pointed form.

P04-005.boundary_rationale: Every reference in this row touches the ch 20/21 numbering shift and is written dual. Onset: the strict word-event formula at web:Ezek.20.45 = oshb:Ezek.21.1 (וַיְהִ֥י דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר), a hard seam. MT 20:44 is followed by a pe (single witness), corroborating the onset at MT 21:1. Close: web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5 (וָאֹמַ֕ר אֲהָ֖הּ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֑ה הֵ֚מָּה אֹמְרִ֣ים לִ֔י הֲלֹ֛א מְמַשֵּׁ֥ל מְשָׁלִ֖ים הֽוּא), the prophet's own outcry, rendered in web:Ezek.20.49 (= oshb:Ezek.21.5) as “Isn’t he a speaker of parables”. The verse names the mashal root, but a reported taunt in the prophet's own mouth is a turn in the account and no close-role formula, so the close's near face carries no licensed signal; a pe stands immediately after it (single-witness) and corroborates that paragraph only. That unlicensed close is what this row's reduced confidence rests on. That pe is also the point where the Masoretic tradition's own paragraph division sits exactly at the WEB's chapter break, so this zone is a seam site and a numbering site at once.
P04-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating web:Ezek.20.45-Ezek.21.5 = oshb:Ezek.21.1-Ezek.21.10 (the mashal plus its plain-sense restatement against the land) as one row was considered and rejected: web:Ezek.21.1 = oshb:Ezek.21.6 opens with its own strict word-event formula, a second hard seam, and the outcry at web:Ezek.20.49 = oshb:Ezek.21.5 already ends the mashal, with a pe standing after it (single-witness).

P04-008.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting a second time at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17, which the WEB renders “Cry and wail, son of man”, was considered and rejected. That verse carries the son-of-man address, one of the 93 verses in that class, and carries no word-event and no messenger formula; the WEB opens no paragraph at it, and translation lineation would not drive a boundary in any case. A further seam was weighed one verse later, from both sides. The verse closing at web:Ezek.21.13 = oshb:Ezek.21.18 ends on the utterance formula (נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה), “says the Lord Yahweh”, with a pe following it in this witness (single witness); the next verse, web:Ezek.21.14 = oshb:Ezek.21.19, opens with the ve'attah, the and-you address “You therefore, son of man, prophesy” (וְאַתָּ֣ה בֶן אָדָ֔ם הִנָּבֵ֕א). Both sides carry real evidence: an utterance-formula close on one side of the seam and, on the other, the ve'attah, an onset-class device that brings the son-of-man address with it. That signature is verse-final, its verse being one of the 81 in the long utterance class, so the second of the two conditions a renewal must meet, the verse before it ending on a close-role formula, is met on the bytes here. What carries the unit past the seam is the shape of the renewal: a ve'attah that renews the command to prophesy to the same addressee, standing after a verse-final utterance signature, is a paragraph and not an onset. The ve'attah is new at MT 21:19, but the address it renews is not: the son-of-man address with the command to prophesy already stands at web:Ezek.21.9 = oshb:Ezek.21.14, where it introduces the book's only messenger formula naming the Lord alone, כֹּ֖ה אָמַ֣ר אֲדֹנָ֑י, and the son-of-man address returns at web:Ezek.21.12 = oshb:Ezek.21.17; and MT 21:19 continues the same sword doubled a third time (וְתִכָּפֵ֞ל חֶ֤רֶב שְׁלִישִׁ֨תָה֙, oshb:Ezek.21.19), the sword already sharpened and polished at oshb:Ezek.21.14-16, rather than opening a new topic.

P06-003.boundary_rationale: Onset: 25:12 opens with the messenger formula and a fresh addressee, "כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה יַ֣עַן עֲשׂ֥וֹת אֱד֛וֹם בִּנְקֹ֥ם נָקָ֖ם לְבֵ֣ית יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֶּאְשְׁמ֥וּ אָשׁ֖וֹם וְנִקְּמ֥וּ בָהֶֽם" (oshb:Ezek.25.12) — Edom — again a messenger-formula addressee-change cut. In the WEB, “Because Edom has dealt against the house of Judah by taking vengeance, and has greatly offended, and taken revenge on them,” (web:Ezek.25.12). Close (both sides): 25:14 ends "וְנָתַתִּ֨י אֶת נִקְמָתִ֜י בֶּאֱד֗וֹם בְּיַד֙ עַמִּ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְעָשׂ֣וּ בֶאֱד֔וֹם כְּאַפִּ֖י וְכַחֲמָתִ֑י וְיָֽדְעוּ֙ אֶת נִקְמָתִ֔י נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14), carrying a PE immediately after. The close itself is a disclosed deviation from the strict recognition formula: the verb clause reads "and they shall know MY VENGEANCE" (an object noun, not "that I am YHWH"), stacked with the utterance-of-the-Lord-YHWH signature, "נְאֻ֖ם אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה" (oshb:Ezek.25.14); it belongs to the utterance list (sweep: 81 verses), not the strict recognition list (sweep: 28 verses) or either 2ms/2mp recognition family. Behind this row, 25:11 closed Moab on the strict 3mp recognition + SAMEKH; ahead, 25:15 opens a fresh messenger formula with the addressee change to the Philistines. Both faces of both seams therefore carry signals the witness counts; what holds this row's confidence lower is the shape of the division itself, which the plan leaves open for these oracles — four short rows, two, or one seventeen-verse row — with this row standing as one of the four.
P06-003.device_notes: 25:14's close names "my vengeance" rather than the strict "that I am YHWH" recognition object, so it is cited here as an utterance-formula close with a recognition-adjacent variant, not quoted as the strict recognition formula. A messenger formula also stands inside the span at 25:13, the turn from the indictment to the verdict; it opens no unit of its own here, since the addressee does not change across 25:12/25:13 and 25:12 does not end on a close-role formula.

P06-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: 26:1 opens "וַיְהִ֛י בְּעַשְׁתֵּֽי עֶשְׂרֵ֥ה שָׁנָ֖ה בְּאֶחָ֣ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1) — a year-and-day dateline whose month is not named (“In the eleventh year, in the first of the month”, web:Ezek.26.1, WEB) together with the PERFECT-form word-event, "הָיָ֥ה דְבַר יְהוָ֖ה אֵלַ֥י לֵאמֹֽר" (oshb:Ezek.26.1), the 7-verse hayah family the dated oracles use after their dateline, a HARD seam and the strongest onset class in the book. In the WEB, “In the eleventh year, in the first of the month, Yahweh’s word came to me, saying,” (web:Ezek.26.1). 26:2 supplies the accusation, "בֶּן אָדָ֗ם יַ֠עַן אֲשֶׁר אָ֨מְרָה צֹּ֤ר עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הֶאָ֔ח נִשְׁבְּרָ֛ה דַּלְת֥וֹת הָעַמִּ֖ים נָסֵ֣בָּה אֵלָ֑י אִמָּלְאָ֖ה הָחֳרָֽבָה" (oshb:Ezek.26.2), quoting Tyre's own "Aha!" against Jerusalem. Close (both sides): 26:6 ends "וּבְנוֹתֶ֨יהָ֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה בַּחֶ֖רֶב תֵּהָרַ֑גְנָה וְיָדְע֖וּ כִּי אֲנִ֥י יְהוָֽה" (oshb:Ezek.26.6), the strict 3mp recognition formula, with a PE immediately after (single-witness). Ahead, 26:7 reopens with a fresh messenger formula ("כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ אֲדֹנָ֣י יְהוִ֔ה הִנְנִ֧י מֵבִ֣יא אֶל צֹ֗ר…", oshb:Ezek.26.7) introducing Nebuchadnezzar's siege — a new speech unit against the same addressee, not an addressee change, which is why it is held as its own row rather than folded in here: the refrain at 26:6 closes THIS unit. The onset's far face is the mid-verse recognition at 25:17 rather than a verse-final close, and the shape of this chapter's division is one the plan leaves open — four messenger units, or one long row — so this row's confidence stays below what its close seam alone would carry.
P06-005.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating all of 26:1-21 as one row was rejected: the chapter reads as four independently marked units (1-6, 7-14, 15-18, 19-21), the first opened by its dateline and word-event and the other three by a messenger formula, each followed by a section mark in this witness (single-witness); the 26:6 recognition-formula-plus-PE close is independently marked and, since a refrain closes the unit before it, belongs to the unit before it, forcing 26:7 to open fresh.
P06-005.device_notes: 26:1's dateline is a hard seam but not a parent seam (the oracles-against-the-nations collection is nation-ordered, not date-ordered). 26:3 carries the “Behold, I am against you” (web:Ezek.26.3, WEB) verdict-onset idiom, הִנְנִ֥י (oshb:Ezek.26.3), disclosed as sub-onset corroboration, not a competing row onset. The internal four-way split of this chapter rests on the bespoke, disclosed rationale above rather than on a forced single reading.

P06-015.boundary_rationale: Onset: 28:24 opens וְלֹֽא יִהְיֶ֨ה ע֜וֹד לְבֵ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Ezek.28.24) with no formula device at all — the turn to Israel inside the Sidon word-event, carried by its content alone; its far face, 28:23, ends verse-final on the strict recognition formula. Close: 28:26 ends on the recognition with its their-God extension, verse-final in effect, and the witness records a samekh after it (single-witness); across that seam 29:1 is a dateline, so the close stands two-faced. Inside the span one licensed rival was weighed: at 28:25 a messenger formula opens, licensed by the verse-final recognition that ends 28:24, וְיָ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֥י אֲנִ֖י אֲדֹנָ֥י יְהוִֽה (oshb:Ezek.28.24), with a samekh recorded after that verse. It is held because the cut would leave 28:24 standing alone as a one-verse row that is no complete word-event unit, and because the plan names 28:24-26 as the coda to Israel. The onset's near face carries no device of any counted class, and that is what this row's confidence records.
P06-015.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 28:24/28:25 instead, so that the coda begins with the messenger formula, was weighed and not taken. That rival is licensed and two-faced: its near face at 28:25 opens on the messenger formula, and its far face, 28:24, ends verse-final on the adonai-form recognition with a samekh recorded after it (single-witness), which is what licenses a messenger formula as a sub-onset. It is held for two stated reasons: the cut would leave 28:24 alone as a one-verse row that is no complete word-event unit of its own, and the plan names 28:24-26 — the three verses whose recognition clauses stand at 28:22, 28:23 and 28:26 — as the coda to Israel. The wider alternative, folding these three verses back into the Sidon oracle at 28:20-23, dissolves this row's own onset seam and is refused on that same naming.
P06-015.device_notes: Inside 28:24-28:26 the witness records a samekh after 28:24 and another after the closing verse (oshb:Ezek.28.26), single-witness, and a paseq within 28:25, count-only, single-witness, with no position claimed inside that verse; no ketiv/qere note and no editors’ note falls in these three verses. The next dateline seam outside this span stands at 29:1, and these three verses close the oracles against the nations without opening what follows them.

P09-002.strongest_rejected_alternative: A split between the stick demonstration and its interpretation, e.g. after web:Ezek.37.20 (“The sticks on which you write will be in your hand before their eyes.” (web:Ezek.37.20)) or after web:Ezek.37.23 (the purification promise). Rejected: reading each section mark as standing on the verse it follows, no samekh or pe falls in this row's INTERIOR, oshb:Ezek.37.15-Ezek.37.27, single-witness. The only marks anywhere in range are the pe recorded on 37.14, behind the onset seam, and the samekh recorded on 37.28, at the close seam. The messenger-formula reopenings at oshb:Ezek.37.19 and oshb:Ezek.37.21 keep the same hearers, and a messenger formula opens a sub-unit only where the addressee changes or where the verse before it ends on a close-role formula: 37:18 and 37:20 end on no formula of any counted class, so neither condition is met here.
P09-002.device_notes: Category disclosure: the 37.15-28 span is anchored on the commanded stick action of 37.16-20, but its interpretation at 37.21-28 carries the burden of a restoration oracle (gather/return, the covenant of peace at 37.26, ‘my servant David’ and ‘my sanctuary’ devices) -- a one-clause category deviation rather than a split: the pe behind it at 37.14 and the samekh closing it at 37.28 are the row's only framing marks, and the addressee stays constant across both halves. 37.16 is a doubled ketiv/qere verse: two notes on one verse, each written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.16, ketiv), and each read as the same consonantal word under different pointing -- the first note reads חֲבֵרָ֑יו and the second חֲבֵרָֽיו, the two differing by exactly one codepoint, U+0591 HEBREW ACCENT ETNAHTA in the first against U+05BD HEBREW POINT METEG in the second (MEASURED by comparing the two readings the K/Q apparatus gives at this verse, codepoint by codepoint; WLC/OSHB, single witness), and 37.19 carries one further note on the same word (written חברו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, ketiv), read חֲבֵרָ֑יו (oshb:Ezek.37.19, Qere)); 37.22 carries a further K/Q note in this span (written יהיה (oshb:Ezek.37.22, ketiv), read יִֽהְיוּ (oshb:Ezek.37.22, Qere)). A boundary is never argued from any of these Qere readings; they are disclosed as textual-variant sites only.

P09-009.device_notes: 39.17 carries two paseq occurrences on the one verse (count-only, single-witness); no K/Q or editorial note falls in this span. The onset is a sub-onset licensed by the addressee change at 39.17, from Gog to the birds and the beasts of the field, and the row is held at medium confidence because the seam behind it carries a mark and no formula. Onset corroboration: one samekh stands after MT 39:16 in this witness, single witness.

P10-008.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 41:12 turns to a different structure from the side-chamber circuit just closed, a change of measured object rather than a bare topic shift: וְהַבִּנְיָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֶל פְּנֵ֨י הַגִּזְרָ֜ה פְּאַ֣ת דֶּֽרֶךְ הַיָּ֗ם (oshb:Ezek.41.12) “The building that was before the separate place at the side toward the west” (web:Ezek.41.12), confirmed by the fresh measuring verb וּמָדַ֣ד אֶת הַבַּ֔יִת (oshb:Ezek.41.13) that opens this row's own accounting of the building. The row carries the temple/separate-place/building triad each measured at a hundred cubits (41:13-14), the rear building and its galleries with a K/Q lexical variant on 'galleries' at oshb:Ezek.41.15 (ואתוקיהא, checked: a form variant, not a numeral), the side-chamber gallery structure (41:16-19), the cherubim-and-palm-tree decorative program running to above the entrance (41:18-20), the doorposts of the nave (41:21), the wooden altar-table with its own speak-formula notice, וַיְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלַ֔י זֶ֚ה הַשֻּׁלְחָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה (oshb:Ezek.41.22), its speech rendered “This is the table that is before Yahweh” (web:Ezek.41.22), opened by the 'spoke to me' root, distinct from the 'said to me' form at 41:4, the double doors of the nave and sanctuary (41:23-25), and the repeated cherubim-and-palm-tree pattern closing on the porch threshold. Close side: 41:26 ends וְצַלְע֥וֹת הַבַּ֖יִת וְהָעֻבִּֽים (oshb:Ezek.41.26), “the side rooms of the temple and the thresholds” (web:Ezek.41.26), and the next verse, oshb:Ezek.42.1, moves the tour out to the outer court with its double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי … וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי -- a strong close by contrast, since the following onset is a transport verse inside the vision, a licensed onset, even though this row's own onset rests on the measured-object change rather than a formula. The puncta extraordinaria at 41:20, וְקִ֖יר הַׄהֵׄיׄכָֽׄלׄ (oshb:Ezek.41.20), five instances of the upper dot U+05C4, are disclosed single-witness as intra-row texture on the decorative program's own close, not as boundary evidence.

P10-010.boundary_rationale: Onset side: 42:1 opens with a double transport verb, וַיּוֹצִאֵ֗נִי אֶל הֶֽחָצֵר֙ הַחִ֣יצוֹנָ֔ה ... וַיְבִאֵ֣נִי אֶל הַלִּשְׁכָּ֗ה (oshb:Ezek.42.1) “he brought me out into the outer court” (web:Ezek.42.1) ... “Then he brought me into the room” (web:Ezek.42.1) -- the strongest onset in the span after 40:1 and 43:1 -- moving the tour to the priests' chambers, first north-side (42:1-9) then, by parallel description, south-side (42:10-12). Close side: 42:13-14 supplies the row's function. The guide's naming speech closes the survey of these rooms by reading and not by formula: the וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) it carries is an onset-type device inside the vision, weighed below, and no close formula at all. These are the holy chambers where the priests “eat the most holy things” (web:Ezek.42.13) and must change garments before approaching the people -- a law-toned close inside a measurement row, disclosed rather than reclassified. The double transport at the onset is a licensed onset inside the vision, a stronger opening than a bare content shift would give; the close rests on the reading above rather than on a formula, and no parashah mark stands anywhere in these chapters to corroborate either edge (single-witness).
P10-010.device_notes: No parashah mark in ch 42. Two K/Q verses disclosed (42:9 doubled, 42:14 single), both checked: neither touches a numeral. Content disclosure, not a category deviation: 42:13-14 states a food-purity law for the chambers just measured; the row is classed temple_measurement because the chamber dimensions (42:1-12) dominate it and the law clause closes rather than opens the unit. Paseq disclosed, count-only, single-witness: three occurrences over two verses (42:10, and two on 42:13); the strokes are not placed within either verse, since the witness's paseq apparatus serves here only as a count by verse. The parallel south-side description at 42:10-12 is the second seam a reader might take, and it is weighed here rather than adopted: it cross-references the north-side rooms, “like the appearance of the rooms which were toward the north” (web:Ezek.42.11), and carries no transport verb of its own.
P10-010.strongest_rejected_alternative: Cutting at 42:12/42:13, where the guide's own וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלַ֗י (oshb:Ezek.42.13) stands at the verse's head, was weighed and not taken. Inside a vision that speech is a licensed onset whoever speaks it, so the rival's near face carries a real signal; its far face, 42:12, ends on the doors of the south-side rooms with no close-role formula, and neither verse carries a section mark. What holds the row against it is that 42:13-14 states the function of the very chambers just measured, so the naming speech completes this survey rather than opening a new one, and taking the cut would leave a two-verse remainder that is no unit of its own.

P11-005.boundary_rationale: Onset: the messenger formula at Ezek.45.9 ('thus says the Lord GOD: enough, princes of Israel') opens a rebuke that closes, within the same verse, on the utterance signature -- an internal quotation-closing device, not a competing row close. The unit covers honest weights and measures (10-12), the fixed grain/oil/flock offering (13-15, utterance signature mid-paragraph at 45.15), and the shared duty of people and prince across the feasts, new moons and Sabbaths (16-17). Close: 45:17 ends on the prince's duty of atonement, with no close-role formula of any counted class; the samekh recorded after that verse (single-witness) corroborates the paragraph and supplies none, so this row closes on an unformulated near face. Ezek.45.17 itself carries the calendrical construction glossed 'at the new moons' -- one of the book's four verses carrying that construction (with Ezek.46.3) -- disclosed explicitly as NOT a date formula and NOT one of the four calendar dates at 45.18/45.20/45.21/45.25, to forestall exactly the confusion those verses invite.
